name: Crazy Solo
description: Crazy Solo (often just called 'Solo' in parts of Eastern Europe and USA) is a trick-taking card game for 3 to 12 players, though 4 is standard. It features a bidding hierarchy where players can 'Go Alone' (Solo) against the others. The game is known for its escalating bids involving specific trump suits (Hearts high) and partnership calling.
deck: 36-card deck (Ace-ten: A,10,K,Q,J,9,8,7,6 per suit); 30-36 cards depending on player count.

history.origins: Derived from L'Hombre via Solo Whist, but with Americanized bidding rules (using Hearts as a premium suit).
timeline: 1950s: Rules codified in Hoyle as 'Solo' (with variations).
Present: A rare gem kept alive by dedicated groups.
history.cultural: Often played with a pot or kitty, adding stakes.
history.evolution: The term 'Crazy' was added to distinguish it from Solo Whist or the shedding game Solo.

setup.players: Three to twelve players; four or more is standard.
setup.deck: 36 cards (standard); 30, 32, 33 or 35 depending on player count.
setup.dealing: All cards distributed one at a time starting with the player to the left of the dealer. With 4, 6, 9 or 12 players use full 36-card deck; with 5 or 7 remove six of spades (35); with 8 remove all sixes (32); with 10 remove all sixes plus seven of spades and seven of clubs (30); with 11 remove sixes of spades, clubs and diamonds (33). Player to dealer's left is on the lead.

rules.objective: The solo team (caller and optional secret partner) aims to win a majority of the 120 card points (61 or more) in tricks; the gang aims to prevent this.
rules.gameplay: Each hand: deal all cards; then a bidding round (Pass, Solo, Solo in Hearts, Go Alone, Go Alone in Hearts) starting with the player on the lead. Each player bids once in turn; each must bid higher than the previous or pass. Winning bidder calls trump (Hearts automatic if bid was Solo in Hearts or Go Alone in Hearts) and, if not going alone, calls a card as partner; the holder of that card is the secret partner. Play: player to dealer's left leads. Players must follow suit if possible; if unable, must play a trump if able. No requirement to beat the card led. Winner of each trick leads the next. Solo team's trick points are combined; 61 or more wins the hand.
keyRules: Card ranking (high to low): Ace, Ten, King, Queen, Jack, 9, 8, 7, 6.
Point values: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2; 9-6 count 0. Total 120 points.
Bids in order: Pass, Solo, Solo in Hearts, Go Alone, Go Alone in Hearts.
Caller may call a card in his own hand to play alone without revealing it.
If all pass, cards are thrown in and the same dealer redeals.

strategy.basic: Bid cautiously. Going Alone is very risky unless you have 6-7 trumps and side Aces. In a partnership bid, signal your partner by leading trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Hearts' Premium: Since Hearts are worth double (or rank higher), aggressive bidding in Hearts can shut out opponents who have strong Spades hands.
strategy.advanced: Defending a Solo: Lead through the Soloist's weakness. If they are void in Clubs, lead Clubs to force a trump. If they lead trumps, hold your winner until the end.
tips: Aces are powerful in Go Alone.
Don't overbid just because you like Hearts.

variations.name: Going Blind
variations.description: Player on the lead may declare blind before looking at cards; if they have at least one heart they must go under (be solo) with Hearts as trump; no other player may bid. If no heart, hand reverts to normal bidding. Typically played once per evening.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant rule-only; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

variations.name: Gang call-out
variations.description: A gang player may call out that the gang is taking the trick to encourage others to dump point-cards; undiscovered partner may bluff by calling gang.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant rule-only; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

scoring.description: Points awarded for making bid. Penalties for failing. Hearts double the stakes.
scoring.winCondition: Solo team wins by taking 61 or more of the 120 card points in tricks.
